title: Infra GPU capacity, networking, IaC & CI/CD runbook
author: Maya Lin
summary: This runbook consolidates operational guidance for Redwood's GPU fleet and capacity planning, cloud accounts and networking guardrails, Terraform/IaC module patterns, and CI/CD pipeline standards. It is intended for oncall engineers, infra owners, and platform teams responsible for maintaining predictable inference capacity and safe deployment workflows.
scope: Covers GPU fleet provisioning and scaling, cross-account networking and peering, Terraform module ownership and patterns, CI/CD build/release pipelines for infra modules, and first-response runbook steps for capacity, networking, and CI failures.
audience: Oncall engineers, infra SREs, platform engineers, infra module authors, release engineers, and solutions engineers supporting Dedicated or Private deployments.
goals: Provide a single source of truth for capacity planning and emergency actions related to the GPU fleet.
Standardize Terraform module layout and promotion paths for infra changes.
Define CI/CD best practices for safe rollouts (canary, staged apply, automated tests).
Document networking and cloud-account guardrails to prevent noisy-neighbor and free-riding incidents.
Reduce time-to-recovery for common incidents with clear, tested runbook steps.
service_slos_and_thresholds: Avg scheduling latency for new inference jobs: < 90s (P99 < 300s)
Provisioned GPU utilization target: 55-75% (buffer of 15% free capacity to absorb spikes)
Cluster GPU CPU memory pressure alert: Node memory > 85% for 5m
Job queue length warning: > 50 pending jobs for 10m
Failover SLO for cross-region capacity fallback: < 2 minutes to route traffic to fallback pools
capacity_planning_guidelines: Monthly forecast process: product teams submit expected QPS and model size changes 3 weeks before quarter start.
Capacity formula (baseline): required_gpus = ceil((expected_avg_tokens_per_minute * safety_factor) / tokens_per_gpu_minute). Use safety_factor=1.3 by default.
Buffer policy: maintain 15% headroom on Dedicated pools and 25% for peak-days during launches.
Reservation policy: convert sustained 30-day average usage > 70% to reserved capacity and notify finance for commit planning.
Spot vs On-demand: Use spot instances for non-latency critical training/aux jobs; inference pools should use on-demand or reserved for SLA-bound customers.
scaling_and_autoscaling_policies: Horizontal scaling: scale-up when avg GPU utilization across pool > 70% for 10 minutes AND queue length > 10.
Scale-down: scale-down when avg GPU utilization < 40% for 20 minutes and no pending high-priority jobs.
Cooldowns: enforce a 10-minute cooldown after any autoscale action to prevent oscillation.
Autoscaler constraints: max_growth_rate = 30% of pool size per 10 minutes; emergency scale-up bypass requires SRE approval.
Pre-warming: schedule pre-warm operations 30 minutes before major product launches based on forecast inputs.
terraform_modules_and_practices: Module layout: modules/networking, modules/gpu-pool, modules/iam, modules/monitoring. Each module has README.md, inputs.tf, outputs.tf, and examples/.
Module ownership: assign a single owner and a secondary reviewer in module's OWNERS file; use CODEOWNERS for repo-level review enforcement.
Promotion flow: feature branch -> PR with plan output -> automated terratest -> canary apply in test account -> apply to staging -> apply to prod via gated approval.
State storage: Terraform state in remote S3 with server-side encryption and state locking via DynamoDB. Ensure env-specific state keys (e.g., state/prod/gpu-pool.tfstate).
Secure secrets: do not store secrets in TF; reference secrets from Vault using the vault provider or template_file with external secret injection at deploy time.
ci_cd_build_and_release: Pipeline layout: lint -> unit tests (tflint/validate) -> plan -> terratest/integration -> gated manual approval -> apply.
Required checks: all PRs modifying modules/** or env/** must have a successful plan and 1+ owner approval before merge.
Canary applies: for infra changes with blast radius > medium, create a canary workspace which applies change to a single non-production account and monitor for 60 minutes.
Rollback strategy: auto-create a backup branch with previous terraform state snapshot before apply; document manual steps to restore state from S3 and re-apply previous config.
Build artifacts: store plan artifacts and terratest results for 90 days for audit and regression analysis.
networking_and_cloud_accounts: Account structure: separate AWS accounts for prod, staging, dev, and shared infra. Use Control Tower or equivalent for baseline guardrails.
VPC design: default VPCs are forbidden for prod. Use segmented subnets by purpose (inference-private, inference-public, tooling-admin).
Peering and transit: prefer Transit Gateway for cross-account routing; document route table entries and tag ownership for each route.
Security groups: deny-all by default; open least-privilege rules with owner/justification tag and TTL for temporary exceptions.
Egress firewalling: enforce egress filtering for private pools and log DNS queries via VPC Flow Logs + central logging account.
runbook_incident_playbook: 1) Detect: Review alert on PagerDuty and check cluster dashboard for GPU utilization, queue length, and recent scaling events.
2) Triage: Identify whether incident is capacity, networking, or CI-related by checking 'gpu-pool' and 'networking' dashboards and recent terraform applies.
3) Immediate mitigation - capacity: if shortage, trigger manual scale-up via admin console (increase pool desired count) and enable emergency_preempt option where available.
4) Immediate mitigation - networking: if VPC/VPN issue, run 'aws ec2 describe-vpn-connections' and verify Transit Gateway attachments; if broken, failover to secondary region per failover runbook.
5) Immediate mitigation - CI/CD: if a bad infra change caused outage, revert via 'terraform apply' using the last known-good state snapshot and comment in PR with root cause.
6) Communicate: post status to #infra-status and notify affected product teams with ETA and mitigation steps.
7) Post-incident: open a postmortem within 48 hours, include timeline, RCA, and action items, assign owners and due dates.
rollout_and_rollback: Canary rollout steps: apply to test workspace -> deploy to a single AZ in staging -> run smoke tests for 30 minutes -> promote to full staging -> schedule prod apply in low-traffic window.
Rollback criteria: failed health checks, increased error rates beyond baseline, provisioning regressions, or rollback requested by SRE/product owner.
Rollback commands: restore state from S3 'aws s3 cp s3://tf-state-prod/backup/<timestamp>.tfstate ./restore.tfstate' and run 'terraform init -force-copy && terraform apply -state=./restore.tfstate'.
Emergency rollback: if terraform state is corrupted, contact state-owners and run the documented emergency state restore playbook.
ownership_and_escalation: Module owners: referenced in module OWNERS file; escalation to infra-leads if owner is unavailable.
Escalation path: oncall -> infra lead -> head of infra -> CTO for >4 hour incidents or customer-impacting outages.
Change windows: non-emergency prod applies between 02:00-05:00 UTC unless otherwise negotiated.
operational_checklist: Weekly: verify healthy headroom in all inference pools and reconcile with forecast.
Weekly: review failed terraform plans and stale feature branches touching modules/**.
Monthly: run terratest suite against staging and update test manifests for new models or instance types.
Quarterly: capacity review with product and finance to discuss committed/dedicated capacity changes.
